# [EPIC] Core Microservices

## Epic
Three business services, each owning its own data and serving a tested REST
API:

- **movie-service** — discovery, search and movie details, TMDB-shaped, stored
  in MongoDB and cached in Redis.
- **user-service** — accounts, JWT login with rotating refresh tokens,
  profile, favorites and watchlist, stored in PostgreSQL.
- **actor-service** — people, filmography, images and search, stored in
  PostgreSQL behind a TMDB-shaped facade.

Plus what proves they work together: the gateway-boundary and full-stack
integration suites, the newman acceptance gate against a running stack, and
SonarQube analysis with an 80% per-module coverage gate.

## Business Value
This is the platform's domain layer. Movie discovery, user accounts and cast
details are the features the frontend renders and the later epics extend; the
gateway, the AI service and the React app all read from these three.

## Product Goal alignment
Direct. The [Product Goal](../../docs/process/PRODUCT_GOAL.md) is a
self-hosted, TMDB-shaped microservices platform, and these three services are
the part of it that holds the domain data.

## Notes
Spring Boot across all three services. Database per service (ADR-002): there
is no shared schema and no cross-service join, so favorites store TMDB movie
ids and nothing more.

actor-service moved from a raw TMDB passthrough (ADR-003) to owning persisted
data behind a TMDB-shaped facade (ADR-010). movie-service serves the same
facade shape for movies.

Detail lives in the two child Stories and their Tasks, not here.
